Rashi on Yevamot 39a:10:1.hebrew: אדמיפלגי בגופה - של קרקע, ולאחר מיתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 39a:10:1.english: Instead of disputing about [the property] itself - [meaning] of the land, and after [her] death.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:10:2.english: Let them dispute during her lifetime and [regarding] the produce - Since the reason is that his hand is like her hand.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:11:1.hebrew: ותו לא מידי - אין להשיב על כך, דודאי דיקא כוותיה, וקשיא ליה מתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 39a:11:1.english: And nothing more - There is nothing to reply to this, for certainly [the Mishnah] is precise according to him, yet [the case where] she died is difficult for him.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:12:1.english: That he divorces her with a bill of divorce - And he does not require ḥalitza.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:12:2.hebrew: ומחזירה - אם רצה, ולא מיתסרא עליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 39a:12:2.english: And takes her back - If he wishes, and she is not forbidden to him.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:13:1.hebrew: ויבמה - אע"פ שלקחה, קרי ליה ויבמה:
Rashi on Yevamot 39a:13:1.english: And consummate the levirate marriage with her - Even though he [already] took her [as a wife], [Scripture] calls it "and consummate the levirate marriage with her."

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:15:1.english: And [why not] say [that it is] indeed so - [This] refers to the entire matter.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:15:2.hebrew: ולקחה לו - ויבמה מצי למכתב, למה לי דכתיב לאשה? ש"מ הרי היא כאשתו. ויבמה, אי לכדרבי בפ"ק (לעיל יבמות דף ח.) — לאסור צרות ועריות; אי לכדרבנן — ויבמה בעל כרחה:
Rashi on Yevamot 39a:15:2.english: And take her to him - [Scripture] could have written [only] "and perform levirate marriage with her"; why do I need [it] to be written "to be a wife"? Learn from this [that] she is like his wife. And [as for] "and perform levirate marriage with her" — either according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] in the first chapter (above, Yevamot 8a) [it comes] to forbid rival wives and forbidden relatives, or according to the Rabbis, "and perform levirate marriage with her" [teaches that he may do so even] against her will.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:16:1.english: A wife was acquired to him - To perform levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:16:2.hebrew: מן השמים - ולא שיעבד נכסיו לכתובתה, ויכול למוכרן בכל עת שירצה:
Rashi on Yevamot 39a:16:2.english: From Heaven - And he did not encumber his property for her marriage contract, and he may sell it whenever he wishes.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:17:1.english: And if she has nothing from the first [husband] - Because he has no property.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:18:1.english: The mitzvah is for the eldest - [Derived] from [the verse], "And it shall be, the firstborn" (Deuteronomy 25).

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:18:2.english: [If] he does not want, etc. - [It] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:19:1.english: [If] he made [it] dependent upon a minor - An actual minor.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:19:2.hebrew: ובגדול - שהיה גדול האחים במדינת הים, ויש לו אח כאן הגדול מן האחין שלפנינו, ותלה גדול האחין שלפנינו בו, לומר: המתינו לו, שהוא גדול ממני, שמא ייבם אותך. והכי מוכח בגמ' דאמרי': ת"ש, ובגדול עד שיבא ממדינת הים אין שומעין לו, ואי ס"ד חליצת גדול עדיפא, אמאי אין שומעין לו? נינטר דלמא אתי וחליץ! אלמא אותו שבמדינת הים גדול שבכל האחין הוא:
Rashi on Yevamot 39a:19:2.english: And upon [his] eldest [brother] - [This means] that the eldest of the brothers was overseas, and he has a brother here who is the eldest of the brothers [present] before us, and the eldest of the brothers [present] before us made [his decision] dependent upon him, saying: "Wait for him, for he is older than me; perhaps he will consummate the levirate marriage with you." And so is it proven in the Gemara, where we say: Come [and] hear: "And upon [his] eldest [brother], until he comes from overseas, they do not listen to him." Now if it should enter your mind [that] ḥalitza of the eldest [brother] is preferable, why do they not listen to him? Let us wait — perhaps he will come and perform ḥalitza! Evidently, the one who is overseas is the eldest of all the brothers.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:19:3.hebrew: עליך מצוה - שאע"פ שאחיך שבמדינת הים גדול ממך, כיון דאתה גדול האחין שלפנינו, עליך מצוה, דשהויי מצוה לא משהינן. והכי מפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Yevamot 39a:19:3.english: [The] mitzva [is] upon you - For even though your brother who is overseas is older than you, since you are the eldest of the brothers before us, the mitzva [is] upon you, for we do not delay a mitzva. And so it is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:1:1.hebrew: וקסבר אביי ידו כידה - מדאוקי פלוגתייהו בנפלו לה תחתיו, ואפי' הכי לבית הלל נכסים בחזקתן, קסבר אביי נשואה ידו כידה ולא יותר. הלכך, כשמת ואין ליבם בה אלא זיקה, ידו גריעא מידה ונכסים בחזקתה. ובית שמאי פליגי ואמרי: נשואה ידו עדיפא מידה, וכשמת, יד היבם כידה ויחלוקו. ובכתובות בהכותב (כתובות דף פג.) נמי פליגי אביי ורבא, דקאמר אביי ידו כידה, ורבא אמר ידו עדיפא מידה, ואמרינן התם: נפקא מינה לשומרת יבם:
Rashi on Yevamot 39a:1:1.english: And Abaye holds [that] his hand is like her hand - Since he established their dispute [as referring to a case] where [the property] fell to her while she was under him [i.e., married to her husband], and even so, according to Beit Hillel, the property [remains] in its presumptive status, Abaye holds [that for] a married woman, his [the husband's] hand is like her hand, and no more. Therefore, when he dies and the yavam has in her only a levirate bond, his hand is weaker than her hand, and the property [remains] in her possession. And Beit Shammai disagree and say [that for] a married woman, his hand is stronger than her hand; and when he dies, the hand of the yavam is like her hand, and they divide [it]. And in Ketubot, in [the chapter] HaKotev (Ketubot 83a), Abaye and Rava also disagree, as Abaye says his hand is like her hand, and Rava says his hand is stronger than her hand; and we say there [that] the practical difference [applies] to a woman awaiting a yavam.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:20:1.hebrew: ביאת קטן וחליצת גדול - גדול רוצה לחלוץ, וקטן [ממנו] רוצה לייבם. והאי קטן לאו קטן ממש הוא, דקטן לאו בר חליצה וייבום הוא, שמא ימצא סריס; ואפי' מאן דלא חייש למיעוט וקטן מותר לייבם, הכא ודאי סוגיא דשמעתין מוכחא דלאו קטן ממש הוא, מדקפריך לקמן: תלה בקטן עד שיגדיל, ושני ליה: שהויי מצוה לא משהינן, אלמא בקטן ממש כולהו מודו:
Rashi on Yevamot 39a:20:1.english: Consummation of [marriage by] a younger [brother] or ḥalitza [performed by] an eldest [brother] - The eldest [brother] wants to perform ḥalitza, and a [brother] younger [than him] wants to perform levirate marriage. And this "younger" [brother] is not an actual minor, for a minor is not eligible for ḥalitza or levirate marriage, lest he be found [to be] a eunuch; and even [according to] the one who is not concerned for a minority [possibility] and [holds that] a minor is permitted to perform levirate marriage, here, certainly, the passage of our discussion proves that he is not an actual minor, from the fact that [the Gemara] asks later on: "[What if] it depends on a minor until he grows up?" and answers it: "We do not delay [the fulfillment of] a mitzva" — evidently, regarding an actual minor, everyone agrees.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:21:1.english: In the presence of [the] eldest [brother], consummation by [a] younger [brother] is nothing - For the mitzva rests upon the eldest [brother].

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:22:1.english: Rather [he wishes] to perform ḥalitza, and it teaches: [they] go around to all the brothers - Perhaps [one of them] will consummate the levirate marriage with her.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:23:1.hebrew: ואמאי חוזרין אצל גדול - אי אמרת בשלמא דכל "לא רצה" ו"רצו" דמתניתין אייבום קאי, להכי חוזרין אצל גדול, דכיון דכולהו בעו למיחלץ ואיהו נמי בעי למיחלץ, איהו קדים. אלא אי אמרת אפילו מיחלץ לא בעי, אמאי חוזרין אצל גדול? פשיטא דלמכפייה למיחלץ! ונכפינן לדידהו, ולא נטרח ב"ד כולי האי:
Rashi on Yevamot 39a:23:1.english: And why do they return to the eldest - It is well if you say that every [instance of] "he did not want" and "they wanted" in our Mishnah refers to levirate marriage; for that reason they return to the eldest, because since all of them want to perform ḥalitza and he also wants to perform ḥalitza, he takes precedence. But if you say [that] he does not even want to perform ḥalitza, why do they return to the eldest? Obviously, [it is] to force him to perform ḥalitza! [Rather,] let us force them, so that the court will not have to trouble itself so much.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:2:1.english: That his hand is stronger than her hand - And even Beit Hillel agree that the husband's heirs take [a share] in the property.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:3:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן אלא אידי ואידי דנפלו לה כשהיא שומרת יבם רישא דלא עבד בה מאמר - קודם שנפלו לה הנכסים, הלכך זיקה לא מהניא ולא מידי בנכסים:
Rashi on Yevamot 39a:3:1.english: So we read: Rather, both this and that [concern cases in] which [property] fell to her when she was a widow waiting for her yavam; the first clause [concerns a case in] which he had not performed ma'amar [levirate betrothal] with her - before the property fell to her; therefore, the levirate bond is of no avail whatsoever with respect to the property.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:3:2.hebrew: וסיפא דעבד בה מאמר - ובית שמאי לטעמייהו דאמרי מאמר קני, בפרק ארבעה אחין (לעיל יבמות כט.): בית שמאי אומרים אשתו עמו כו'. וב"ה לטעמיהו דאמרי לא קני:
Rashi on Yevamot 39a:3:2.english: And the latter clause [is a case] where he performed ma'amar with her - And Beit Shammai follow their own reasoning, as they say [that] ma'amar acquires [her], in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achin (above, Yevamot 29a): "Beit Shammai say: His wife is with him, etc." And Beit Hillel follow their own reasoning, as they say [that] it does not acquire [her].

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:4:1.hebrew: וקסבר רבא - קנין מאמר לב"ש קני כודאי ארוסה וכספק נשואה. כלומר, אע"ג דב"ש ודאי ארוסה משוי לה לדחות בצר' אחותה משום אחות אשה, כדקתני "אשתו עמו", מיהו לא כודאי נשואה משוי לה למיקני יבם כולה ירושה דילה, אלא כספק נשואה, ויחלוקו:
Rashi on Yevamot 39a:4:1.english: And Rava holds - The acquisition of ma'amar [levirate betrothal] according to Beit Shammai acquires [her] as a definite betrothed woman and as an uncertain married woman. That is to say, even though Beit Shammai treat her as a definite betrothed woman to push aside her sister's rival wife on account of [the prohibition of] a wife's sister, as [the Mishnah] teaches, "his wife is with him," nevertheless they do not treat her as a definite married woman for the yavam to acquire all of her inheritance; rather, [they treat her] as an uncertain married woman, and they divide [it].

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:5:1.english: In accordance with Abaye - That the latter clause [of the Mishnah deals] with [a case where property] fell to her while she was under [the authority of] the husband.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:8:1.english: That "she died" is difficult - [The Gemara] explains [this] below.

Rashi on Yevamot 39a:9:1.english: And leave the domain of the husband - When she dies. Evidently, they fell to her [while she was] under her husband.

Tosafot on Yevamot 39a:16:1.hebrew: אשה הקנו לו מן השמים - וא"ת: ומה מרויח בכך היבם, כיון דאי לית לה מראשון תקינו לה רבנן משני? וכ"ת שאם מכר הראשון נכסיו, טרפא מלקוחות אע"פ שיש בני חורין לשני — א"כ תהא קלה בעיניו להוציאה! ואר"י דנפקא מינה שיכול היבם למכור שדותיו, ואפילו אשתדוף אחר כך שדות של מת, לא טרפא ממשעבדי; ואם היתה אשתו, טורפת מהן. ומיהו למאי דבעי למימר בס"פ מי שהיה נשוי (כתובות צה. ושם) דאי אשתדוף בני חרי לא טרפא ממשעבדי — קשה. וי"ל דנפקא מינה אם גירשה ואח"כ אשתדוף שדותיו של מת, דלא גביא מבני חרי דשני:
Tosafot on Yevamot 39a:16:1.english: A wife was acquired to him by Heaven - And if you ask: What does the yavam gain by this, since if she does not have [property from which to collect] from the first [husband], the Rabbis instituted for her [to collect] from the second [husband]? And if you say that if the first [husband] sold his property, she seizes [it] from the purchasers even though the second [husband] has unencumbered property — if so, she would be light in his eyes to divorce her! And Ri says that the practical difference is that the yavam can sell his fields, and even if the deceased's fields are subsequently blighted, she does not seize from [the yavam's] encumbered property; whereas if she were his [ordinary] wife, she would seize from them. However, according to what [the Gemara] wants to say at the end of the chapter Mi Shehayah Nasui (Ketubot 95a and there), that if unencumbered property is blighted one does not seize from encumbered property, [this] is difficult. And one can say that the practical difference is if he divorced her and afterwards the deceased's fields were blighted, that she does not collect from the unencumbered property of the second [husband].

Tosafot on Yevamot 39a:19:1.hebrew: ובחרש ושוטה - מדלא קאמר "עד שיתרפא", משמע דאפי' תלה לייבם לאלתר אין שומעין, לפי שאין חוסמין אותה. וה"ה דה"מ למינקט מוכה שחין:
Tosafot on Yevamot 39a:19:1.english: And [upon] a deaf-mute or an imbecile - Since it does not say "until he is healed," it implies that even if he made [it] dependent [upon them] to perform levirate marriage immediately, we do not listen [to him], because we do not compel her [to marry him]. And the same applies that [the Mishnah] could have mentioned one afflicted with boils.

Tosafot on Yevamot 39a:23:1.hebrew: גבי אחין לא רצו לא לייבם ולא לחלוץ אמאי חוזרין כו' - אפילו לא רצו לייבם אלא לחלוץ, ה"מ למיפרך:
Tosafot on Yevamot 39a:23:1.english: "With the brothers: they wanted neither to perform levirate marriage nor to perform ḥalitzah; why do we return, etc." - Even if they did not want to perform levirate marriage, only ḥalitzah, [the Gemara] could have raised this objection:

Tosafot on Yevamot 39a:4:1.hebrew: וספק נשואה לחלוק בנכסים - לעיל פ' ד' אחין (יבמות דף כט: ושם), גרס רבה גבי מאמר לב"ש: "נישואין עושה או אירוסין עושה", דמתוך תשובתו משמע דמודה דאין יורשה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 39a:4:1.english: "And [she has the status of] an uncertainly married woman, to divide the property" - Above, in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achim (Yevamot 29b, and [see] there), the reading is "Rabbah" regarding ma'amar according to Beit Shammai: "Does it effect marriage or does it effect betrothal?" — for from his response it is implied that he concedes that [the yavam] does not inherit from her.

Tosafot on Yevamot 39a:8:1.hebrew: אע"ג דקשיא מתה - לרבא ניחא, דדוקא לאחר מיתה מהני מאמר לחלוק בנכסים, אבל מחיים לא, דהויא לה איהי ודאי ואינהו ספק. ומ"מ לא בעי רישא לאוקמי בעבד בה מאמר, דמשום דהויא איהי ודאי אין נראה לרבא דתמכור לכתחלה, להכי מוקי לה בלא עבד בה מאמר; אע"ג דלרבה דלעיל מוכרת לכתחלה משום האי טעמא, משום דהויא איהי ודאי — רבא לית ליה האי סברא. בהלכות פסוקות דרב יודאי גאון פסיק כאביי, דרב פפא בתראה קאי כוותיה; והא דלא חשיב ביע"ל קג"ם, משום דאיירי בה אמוראי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 39a:8:1.english: Even though [the case of] "she died" is difficult - For Rava it is satisfactory, since specifically after [her] death ma'amar is effective for [the brothers] to divide the property, whereas during [her] lifetime it is not [effective], because she is a certainty and they are uncertain. And nevertheless, he does not want to establish the first clause [of the Mishnah] as [referring to a case] where he performed ma'amar with her, because [merely] on account of [the fact] that she is a certainty, it does not seem [right] to Rava that she may sell ab initio; therefore he establishes it as [a case] where he did not perform ma'amar with her. Even though according to Rabbah above she may sell ab initio for this reason — because she is a certainty — Rava does not hold this reasoning. In Halakhot Pesukot of Rav Yehudai Gaon, he rules like Abaye, since Rav Pappa, [who is] later, stands in accordance with him; and that which [this dispute] is not counted in Ya'al Kegam is because [later] Amoraim discussed it.
